Bradford's population increased by around 24,000 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 550,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Bradford increased by 4.6%, from around 522,500 in 2011 to around 546,400 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of Yorkshire and The Humber (3.7%), but by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Bradford was home to around 10.6 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 10.2 in 2011. This area was the third-most densely populated local authority area across Yorkshire and The Humber (after Kingston upon Hull and Sheffield).

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Bradford than across Yorkshire and The Humber

Median age increased

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Bradford increased by two years, from 34 to 36 years of age.

This area had the joint lowest average (median) age in Yorkshire and The Humber (alongside Kingston upon Hull and Leeds) and a lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by just over 11,000 (an increase of 31.0%), while the number of residents aged 4 years and under fell by around 5,100 (12.3% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 1.7 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

More lone parents

Bradford saw England's joint third-largest percentage-point rise (alongside Walsall) in the proportion of lone-parent households (from 11.1% in 2011 to 13.1% in 2021).

England's largest increases in the percentage of lone-parent households occurred in Thurrock (from 11.2% to 13.5%) followed by Isles of Scilly (from 3.4% to 5.6%).

Because of its small size, comparisons to Isles of Scilly should be made with caution.

The percentage of households including a lone parent in Bradford increased by 2.0 percentage points

Rise in private renting

Bradford saw Yorkshire and The Humber's largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of privately-rented homes (from 18.1% in 2011 to 23.0% in 2021).

Doncaster saw Yorkshire and The Humber's next largest increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes (from 14.8% in 2011 to 19.4% in 2021).

Every local authority area across Yorkshire and The Humber saw a rise in the percentage of privately-rented homes, as the regional percentage grew from 15.9% to 19.4%.

Private renting in Bradford increased by 4.9 percentage points

Religion in Bradford

In 2021, 28.2% of Bradford residents reported having "No religion", up from 20.7% in 2011. The rise of 7.6 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Bradford. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across Yorkshire and The Humber, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 25.9% to 39.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 33.4% of people in Bradford described themselves as Christian (down from 45.9%), while 30.5% described themselves as Muslim (up from 24.7% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 28.2% of usual residents in Bradford reported having "No religion"

Bradford residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 437,800 Bradford residents said they were born in England. This represented 80.1% of the local population. The figure has risen from just under 425,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 81.4% of Bradford's population.

Pakistan was the next most represented, with around 45,400 Bradford residents reporting this country of birth (8.3%). This figure was up from just over 40,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 7.7% of the population of Bradford.

The number of Bradford residents born in countries that joined the EU between April 2001 and March 2011 (other than Poland, Croatia, Lithuania and Romania) rose from around 5,400 in 2011 (1.0% of the local population) to around 8,300 in 2021 (1.5%).

In 2021, 80.1% of Bradford residents reported their country of birth as England

More people looking after their family or home

Bradford saw Yorkshire and The Humber's largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of people who were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home (from 6.1% in 2011 to 8.1% in 2021).

Kingston upon Hull (from 4.6% to 5.9%) and Calderdale (from 3.6% to 4.8%) saw Yorkshire and The Humber's next largest increases in the percentage of people who were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home.

Every local authority area across Yorkshire and The Humber saw a rise in the percentage of people who were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home, as the regional percentage grew from 3.9% to 4.9%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were looking after their family or home (economically inactive) in Bradford increased by 2.0 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 9.9% of Bradford residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 9.1% in 2011.

In 2021, around 1 in 13 people (7.7%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 9.6% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 58.2% to 58.5%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was 9.7% (similar to 2011) across Yorkshire and The Humber. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Bradford increased by 0.8 percentage points

Disability in Bradford

Bradford saw Yorkshire and The Humber's largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little (from 10.7% in 2011 to 10.0% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

Barnsley (from 11.8% to 11.5%) and Doncaster (from 11.2% to 10.9%) saw Yorkshire and The Humber's next largest decreases in the proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little.

Across Yorkshire and The Humber, the proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little increased from 10.5% to 10.7%, while the proportion in nearby Leeds increased from 10.3% to 10.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a little in Bradford decreased by 0.7 percentage points

Health in Bradford

In 2021, 42.4% of Bradford residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 40.0% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 36.6% to 35.7%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Bradford residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 1.6%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 5.5% to 5.2%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in good health in Bradford decreased by 0.9 percentage points

Change in unpaid care

Bradford saw Yorkshire and The Humber's second-largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing between 20 and 49 hours of weekly unpaid care (from 1.7% in 2011 to 2.4% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

Across the region, only North East Lincolnshire saw a greater rise in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing between 20 and 49 hours of weekly unpaid care (from 1.4% to 2.2%).

Every local authority area across Yorkshire and The Humber saw a rise in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing between 20 and 49 hours of weekly unpaid care, as the regional proportion grew from 1.6% to 2.0%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of those providing between 20 and 49 hours of weekly unpaid care in Bradford increased by 0.7 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Bradford

In 2021, 32.1% of Bradford residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 26.8% in 2011. The 5.3 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across Yorkshire and The Humber, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 7.3% to 8.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 61.1% of people in Bradford identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 67.4% in 2011), while 2.7% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 2.5% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 1.5% in 2011 to 2.0% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

Read the bulletin Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 32.1% of usual residents in Bradford identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

National identity in Bradford

In 2021, 8.8% of Bradford residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 8.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.9%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.9% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Bradford that identified as "British only" increased from 28.0% to 65.1%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across Yorkshire and The Humber (1.6 percentage points, from 5.1% to 6.7%) than in Bradford (0.8 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Bradford increased by 0.8 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Bradford residents aged 16 years and over, 36.9% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 33.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (45.8%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 48.5% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Bradford that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership remained at 8.6%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership in Bradford (3.9 percentage points) was similar to the increase across Yorkshire and The Humber (3.8 percentage points, from 33.9% to 37.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Bradford increased by 3.9 percentage points
